recaps.intro: Polish officials said three more people were found dead at the home of the suspect in Saturday's shooting in Krakow's Main Market Square, after six people were killed and others were wounded in the square.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Three more people were found dead at the home of the suspect in the Krakow market square shooting, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said
bullets.note: The discovery came after police identified the gunman and searched his home later Saturday

bullets.text: The bodies were two women and a man; Tusk said there was much to suggest they were the suspect's immediate family
bullets.note: Officials have not publicly detailed how the three died

bullets.text: Six people were killed and 15 others wounded when a gunman opened fire from a car in Krakow's Main Market Square
bullets.note: Reuters said police shot and arrested the suspect after he fired randomly from a car

bullets.text: Poland's interior minister said the attacker appeared fascinated by far-right ideologies and held ultra-nationalist views
bullets.note: Tusk called the attack terrorism, and Krakow declared a period of mourning through Wednesday

recaps.title: Evening wrap
recaps.intro: A shooting in Krakow remained the day's dominant story after more bodies were found at the suspect's home. Israel's president tasked an opposition leader with forming a government, and Washington saw a round of personnel and legal moves.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: A gunman killed six people and wounded 15 in Krakow's Main Market Square; three more were found dead at the suspect's home
bullets.note: Police shot the suspect and took him into custody after he fired from a car in the historic square

bullets.text: Israel's president tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government after last month's election
bullets.note: Eisenkot will have 28 days, with a possible extension, in a setback for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu

bullets.text: Trump said he offered UFC chief executive Dana White the role of White House press secretary
bullets.note: Trump announced the offer on social media Saturday

bullets.text: Trump ordered the Justice Department to look into Democrats he accused of threatening people
bullets.note: He directed the department to investigate what he called a criminal act, without providing evidence

bullets.text: The U.S. military said it disabled a cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman
bullets.note: Reuters reported the U.S. military said it disabled the vessel

bullets.text: Houston's mayor curtailed police cooperation with ICE, saying elections matter
bullets.note: Reuters reported the mayor was limiting how local police work with immigration agents

bullets.text: The U.S. military announced a new task force aimed at restricting Iran's overland weapons routes
bullets.note: The effort targets land borders and the Caspian Sea as well as prohibited materials

bullets.text: Three people were indicted in a scheme that used AI to impersonate executives and steal about $129 million
bullets.note: Prosecutors charged them with wire fraud and aggravated identity theft

bullets.text: A Houthi-run health ministry said airstrikes it blamed on Saudi Arabia killed 27 people near Yemen's capital
bullets.note: Reuters attributed the death toll to the Houthi-run health ministry

bullets.text: Six House members accused of sexual misconduct or domestic abuse have now lost their seats
bullets.note: Two resigned, one did not run again, one lost a primary, and two were defeated on Tuesday

bullets.text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces a congressional probe over alleged Chinese spy ties
bullets.note: Axios reported that Congress will investigate the allegations

bullets.text: Pedro Alliana was sworn in as president of Paraguay after a banking scandal led to his predecessor's impeachment
bullets.note: The swearing-in followed the impeachment of the previous president over a banking scandal

recaps.title: Culture & entertainment
recaps.intro: The New York Times moved closer to a deal for Letterboxd, Salon ended a 31-year run, opera star Martina Arroyo died at 90, and studios, musicians and animators wrestled with AI and politics.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: The New York Times is in advanced talks to buy film site Letterboxd for a reported $330 million
bullets.note: Deadline said A24 had dropped out, leaving the Times as the leading bidder

bullets.text: Salon said it was ceasing publication after a 31-year run as one of the first online news outlets
bullets.note: The site launched in 1995 and wrote that the web was a very different place then

bullets.text: Opera soprano Martina Arroyo, among the first generation of Black operatic stars, has died at 90
bullets.note: She appeared on many of the world's great stages in a celebrated international career

bullets.text: Christopher Nolan said the Directors Guild is holding studios to account for protecting films from AI
bullets.note: He said The Odyssey includes language warning that the film cannot be used as AI training data

bullets.text: Macklemore said nine U.S. venues turned down his Free Palestine benefit tour
bullets.note: He said dates were offered, then pulled once venues learned the shows were Palestine benefits

bullets.text: Pokemon anime studio OLM trained an AI coloring tool on just three hand-painted frames
bullets.note: The Japan-backed project learns a show's look in about 90 seconds and then colors later frames

bullets.text: Paris Jackson is suing to have executors of Michael Jackson's estate release $600 million into a family trust
bullets.note: ABC News reported she filed the suit demanding the money be moved into the trust

bullets.text: U2 guitarist The Edge wrote a sequel to Elf that never happened, actor Andy Richter said
bullets.note: Richter said the project was fully written at one point but petered out

bullets.text: Evan Gershkovich discussed his 491 days in a Russian prison and his new book This Cursed Beautiful Land
bullets.note: The Wall Street Journal reporter continued reporting from prison, he told Reuters

recaps.title: Science & space
recaps.intro: NASA opened a new astronaut class as it plans a lunar base, October set a global heat record, SpaceX aimed Starship at a mid-November flight, and labs reported finds from ice-cold atoms to ancient footprints.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: NASA is accepting applications through Dec. 3 for a new astronaut class to help grow the Artemis program
bullets.note: The agency has 32 active astronauts and aims to pick the class by late 2027

bullets.text: SpaceX said Starship Flight 15 is targeting a launch as early as Friday, Nov. 13, pending approval
bullets.note: The company said the flight is preparing for a catch of the booster

bullets.text: Last month was the warmest October on record globally, according to the Copernicus Climate Change Service
bullets.note: It was the third straight month above the Paris Agreement warming threshold, the European agency said

bullets.text: Prehistoric footprints may be among the strongest evidence yet that humans reached the Americas earlier than thought
bullets.note: The report described the footprints as some of the strongest evidence yet for an earlier arrival

bullets.text: Researchers reported seeing DNA travel between human cells along tiny tunnels called tunneling nanotubes
bullets.note: Until now, no one had observed that kind of DNA transfer along those intercellular highways

bullets.text: A magnet barely wider than a human hair is among the fastest spinning objects ever recorded
bullets.note: New Scientist said it could be useful for fundamental physics experiments and quantum technology

bullets.text: Scientists cooled a collection of atoms to about 10 picokelvins, barely above absolute zero
bullets.note: The atoms formed a Bose-Einstein condensate colder than any reported before

bullets.text: Data from the Large Hadron Collider showed evidence of a long-sought particle process at extremely small scales
bullets.note: Researchers said the finding is a guide into the smallest scales ever probed

bullets.text: A small wireless implant cleared extra sugar from the blood of mice with type 2 diabetes and obesity
bullets.note: Scientists said the device did the work in animals without relying on conventional medicines

bullets.text: A frequently visited cave wall in Spain revealed rock art engravings thought to be at least 19,000 years old
bullets.note: The assembly of engravings had gone unrecognized despite many people passing the wall

recaps.title: Pictures of the day
recaps.intro: A sunset Falcon 9 launch off the California coast, a backlit view of Saturn's moon Enceladus, and Vermont ridges standing above a sea of clouds.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: A Falcon 9 rocket climbs from a California coastal pad at sunset, trailing fire above a surge of smoke beside the tower
bullets.note: SpaceX posted launch photos after Falcon 9 sent the USSF-432 mission to orbit from pad 4E

bullets.text: Saturn's moon Enceladus appears as a dark disk sitting on glowing, backlit rings, with faint ice jets and a tiny moon nearby
bullets.note: Hadfield shared a NASA view of Enceladus and noted water-ice jets and tiny moon Pandora

bullets.text: Vermont mountain ridges rise through a blanket of low clouds under a blue sky, with evergreens in the foreground
bullets.note: The National Weather Service in Burlington said Mt. Mansfield sat above the cloud sea

recaps.title: Breaking
recaps.intro: A gunman opened fire in Krakow's crowded Main Market Square on Saturday, and the death toll has risen through the morning as police reported more victims.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: At least six people are dead and 15 wounded after a gunman opened fire in a busy market square in Krakow, Poland
bullets.note: Early reports put the toll at two dead, then five, before authorities raised it to at least six

bullets.text: Police shot the gunman and took him into custody after the attack in the Main Market Square in Krakow
bullets.note: The shooting hit the historic heart of Poland's second-largest city

recaps.title: Politics & Washington
recaps.intro: Washington spent Saturday absorbing Stephen Miller's promotion and Trump's take on the midterm losses, while late race calls, ballot fights and agency shake-ups filled out the post-election picture.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Stephen Miller calls his promotion to White House chief of staff the honor of his life at a Mar-a-Lago event
bullets.note: Miller replaces Susie Wiles as Trump's top aide just days after Republicans lost Congress

bullets.text: Trump points to higher oil prices and stalled Senate legislation as reasons for Republicans' midterm losses
bullets.note: His first public read on the defeat came from Mar-a-Lago on Friday

bullets.text: Justice Department asks to dismiss its own lawsuit that sought to stop California from counting about 20,000 ballots
bullets.note: The suit had alleged the ballots went to noncitizens and sought to hold them until statuses were verified

bullets.text: Mary Peltola's campaign sues Alaska over rejected absentee ballot records
bullets.note: Opens a legal fight over ballots in Alaska as post-election counting continues

bullets.text: Former West Virginia governor and longtime U.S. senator Jay Rockefeller has died at 89
bullets.note: He became a leading voice on health care and education during decades in the Senate

bullets.text: Secretary of State Marco Rubio warns top staff against conflicts of interest as Republicans look to 2028, Reuters reports
bullets.note: Comes as Rubio draws attention as a possible future Republican standard-bearer

bullets.text: Trump administration considers a major reorganization of the National Park Service and Fish and Wildlife Service
bullets.note: Internal documents describe the possible overhaul, the Washington Post reports

bullets.text: Congressional critics warn a defiant Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth could imperil military funding
bullets.note: Raises the stakes of the Hegseth fight as Democrats prepare to control the purse strings

bullets.text: A Venezuelan national is arrested in a stolen vehicle near the White House with several firearms
bullets.note: Details come from a criminal complaint and the Department of Homeland Security

bullets.text: Democratic Rep. Aisha Wahab wins reelection in California's 14th District, CBS News projects
bullets.note: She beat fellow Democrat Melissa Hernandez in a rematch of August's special election

bullets.text: The Democratic wave that flipped Congress also reshaped several state legislatures with historic shifts in power
bullets.note: Shows the midterm swing reached well below the federal level

recaps.title: World
recaps.intro: Paraguay's political and banking crisis produced a new president, Russia pounded Kyiv's power grid, and the U.S. kept up limited strikes and pressure on Iran.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Pedro Alliana is sworn in as Paraguay's president as impeached predecessor Santiago Peña is put under house arrest
bullets.note: The crisis was triggered by the collapse of digital bank ueno; Peña was later questioned by prosecutors

bullets.text: Trump confirms the U.S. carried out minor strikes in Iran after state media reported missiles hitting Qeshm Island
bullets.note: Qeshm sits on the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint at the center of the conflict

bullets.text: Expanding its naval blockade, the U.S. military looks to restrict Iranian land commerce, Reuters reports
bullets.note: Would widen economic pressure on Iran beyond the sea routes

bullets.text: Russia hits Kyiv with 36 missiles and drones, injuring several people and partially destroying a kindergarten
bullets.note: Strikes on critical infrastructure brought new power and water outages to the capital

bullets.text: Protests and worker strikes over the cost of living spread across France into the weekend
bullets.note: Demonstrators are also calling for better public services

bullets.text: Pope Leo opens his South America trip in Uruguay, greeting crowds in Montevideo
bullets.note: First day of a papal tour of the region

bullets.text: Egypt reopens its embassy in Libya's capital Tripoli after a 12-year closure
bullets.note: Marks a diplomatic step back into Libya after more than a decade

bullets.text: Syria denies plans to send troops to Yemen as its military ties with Saudi Arabia deepen
bullets.note: Follows reports of Syrian military help to Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks

bullets.text: A Guatemalan lawmaker and three police officers are killed in an armed attack
bullets.note: A deadly attack on a sitting member of Guatemala's congress

bullets.text: Heavy rain floods displacement camps in Gaza City, soaking families' bedding and belongings
bullets.note: Adds to hardship for displaced Palestinians as winter approaches

bullets.text: Rubio will travel to Paris next week to meet G7 foreign ministers
bullets.note: First G7 diplomatic gathering for the U.S. since the midterms

recaps.title: Markets & money
recaps.intro: An AI-driven selloff dominated the week, leaving the Nasdaq with a fourth straight weekly loss despite a Friday bounce. Strong U.S. hiring, a giant crypto hack and weak spots abroad rounded it out.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Nasdaq rebounds Friday but still posts a fourth straight weekly decline
bullets.note: Friday's chip bounce was not enough to erase the week's AI-driven losses

bullets.text: Months of unease over Wall Street's AI boom erupted into a global market convulsion this week, Bloomberg reports
bullets.note: The AI trade has helped power stock prices, corporate spending and economic growth

bullets.text: At the Nov. 5 correction low the S&P 500 was 6% below its record and the Nasdaq 100 15% below
bullets.note: Chip stocks fell much harder, with Nvidia 26% and Micron 48% under their highs

bullets.text: October jobs report shows hiring accelerated, the first major economic snapshot since the midterms
bullets.note: Stocks have seesawed in response to the election results

bullets.text: Binance's chief financial officer is leaving days after hackers stole more than 6 billion dollars in crypto from the exchange
bullets.note: The theft at the world's largest crypto exchange shook the industry this week

bullets.text: Berkshire Hathaway steps up stock buybacks as its operating profit falls
bullets.note: WSJ reports quarterly net income fell 28% as investment gains slumped and insurance profits dropped

bullets.text: Mentions of inflation on S&P 500 earnings calls reach the highest level in more than two years
bullets.note: Signals growing corporate worry over rising costs and weakening consumer confidence

bullets.text: ECB President Christine Lagarde says inflation is likely to remain high in the near future
bullets.note: She added that second-round effects so far are no worse than expected

bullets.text: The Canadian dollar heads for its biggest weekly loss since late September after weak jobs data
bullets.note: The employment miss deepened concerns about Canada's economic outlook

bullets.text: Argentine global bonds head for their worst week in over a year
bullets.note: A global retreat from risk met investor anxiety over next year's presidential election

recaps.title: Morning briefing
recaps.intro: Overnight news centered on Ukraine war talks, Iran pressure and the fallout from the Democratic midterm sweep. Abroad, Paraguay swore in a new president and courts in Kenya and Tanzania handed down heavy sentences.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Missile explosions hit Kyiv, wounding at least five, as Ukraine prepares for new talks with Russia and the US next week
bullets.note: Attack lands days before a fresh round of three-way negotiations

bullets.text: Trump says Russia and Ukraine for the first time want to settle and that a deal could involve all of Europe
bullets.note: Trump made the remarks to reporters on Friday

bullets.text: US Central Command offers up to 20 million dollars and possible relocation for information on Iran's nuclear program
bullets.note: Reward covers Iran's nuclear facilities, equipment or personnel

bullets.text: Venezuelan national arrested sitting in a stolen vehicle near the White House with several firearms
bullets.note: Charges are laid out in a criminal complaint, according to ABC and the Department of Homeland Security

bullets.text: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis is preparing to run for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, Washington Post reports
bullets.note: Florida was one of the few conservative strongholds to survive the Democrats' midterm sweep

bullets.text: Watchdogs say Hegseth's taxpayer-funded video attacking Democrats probably violated federal law
bullets.note: Government employees and resources were used to make the self-promoting video, watchdogs said

bullets.text: DC officials ask incoming Democratic governors to pull their National Guard troops from the capital
bullets.note: The request follows Democratic wins in governor races in Tuesday's midterms

bullets.text: Paraguay swears in Alliana as president after the Senate impeaches President Pena
bullets.note: Pena was placed under house arrest after the impeachment, Reuters reports

bullets.text: Haiti's prime minister says gang leader Mathias Saintil is dead
bullets.note: The death was announced by Haiti's prime minister, Reuters reports

bullets.text: Kenya cult leader Paul Nthenge Mackenzie, convicted of murdering 191 people, sentenced to 200 years in prison
bullets.note: All but one of the victims were children

bullets.text: Tanzania opposition leader Tundu Lissu sentenced to four years in prison for incitement
bullets.note: He was acquitted of treason; the charge stems from a statement made before last year's election

bullets.text: Anthrax outbreak kills dozens of hippos in Africa's oldest national park, officials tell ABC News
bullets.note: A major wildlife die-off in a protected park

bullets.text: Tesla's Cybertruck will cease production next year
bullets.note: Ends the run of Tesla's stainless-steel pickup

bullets.text: Law firm Weil Gotshal collapses virtually overnight, sending shock waves through the legal job market
bullets.note: WSJ calls the demise of the large, respected firm without precedent

recaps.title: AI & tech
recaps.intro: Money and infrastructure dominated tech news: OpenAI added 11 billion dollars at a 1.25 trillion valuation while Google, Microsoft and TSMC reshuffled data center and chip plans. A reported Chinese spy plot targeting Nvidia's CEO also drew attention.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: OpenAI gets 11 billion dollars in new funding at a 1.25 trillion dollar valuation, a source tells Reuters
bullets.note: Bloomberg first reported the raise; TechCrunch says the larger round is expected to close in coming weeks

bullets.text: US intelligence warned a woman close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was working for a Chinese spy agency, NYT reports
bullets.note: She was recruited to collect information on Huang, according to the report

bullets.text: Google buys a southeast Wyoming data center site from AI infrastructure firm Crusoe
bullets.note: Crusoe reportedly failed to lock in customers for the project, including Google

bullets.text: Microsoft is winding down an Oracle deal to rent AI cloud capacity, Bloomberg reports
bullets.note: Microsoft had been renting AI cloud capacity from Oracle under the deal

bullets.text: TSMC explores making advanced 3D memory chips at Nvidia's request, The Information reports
bullets.note: Would put TSMC in direct competition with Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron

bullets.text: Google executive Donald Harrison resigns from the SpaceX board after more than a decade
bullets.note: Comes as independent directors weigh Elon Musk's push for a SpaceX merger with Tesla

bullets.text: Tech stocks bounce back Friday from their worst drubbing in more than a year
bullets.note: Underscored investor faith in the AI buildout behind dozens of record closes

bullets.text: OpenAI issues new data center policies days after a Democratic midterm landslide
bullets.note: Many winning Democrats voiced concern about the facilities' local impact

bullets.text: Anthropic IPO valuation expectations come under pressure, Bloomberg Deals reports
bullets.note: Flagged in Bloomberg's daily deals newsletter

bullets.text: Meta rolls out specialized model versions trained with Muse Wonder, adding Active Memory and Active Focus for all users
bullets.note: Brings the features to all Muse and Meta AI users, per The New Stack

bullets.text: Apple says the App Store has over 100,000 apps built for the iPhone Duo
bullets.note: Apple says thousands of optimized apps are being added each day

bullets.text: Activists breach a Microsoft data center construction site as protests spread in Europe
bullets.note: Protests against data center construction are spreading in Europe, Reuters reports

bullets.text: Beijing video-generation startup Sand.ai raises a 200 million dollar Series A+
bullets.note: Brings its funding over the past 10 months to 300 million dollars

bullets.text: Censys finds more than 800 exposed copies of ARTEX, a Chinese-made AI penetration testing tool tied to cyberattacks
bullets.note: The open-source tool has been linked to several attacks since July, TechCrunch reports

recaps.title: Sports
recaps.intro: Luka Doncic's 53-point night led a big NBA Cup Friday, while NFL news turned on the Ravens ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. In Paris, Carlos Alcaraz saved two match points to reach the semifinals as the ATP Finals field was set.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Luka Doncic scores 53 as the Lakers win, the first Laker since Kobe Bryant with 40-plus in four straight games
bullets.note: Lakers moved to No. 1 in the West with a fourth straight win

bullets.text: Doncic joins Wilt Chamberlain as the only players to average 40-plus points through their first nine games
bullets.note: He has 361 points in nine games, 40.1 per game

bullets.text: Victor Wembanyama posts 30 points and 14 rebounds as the Spurs win their seventh straight
bullets.note: San Antonio sits fourth in the West

bullets.text: Celtics win and rise to No. 2 in the East; Thunder, Hawks and Timberwolves extend win streaks
bullets.note: Boston also improved to 2-0 in its NBA Cup group

bullets.text: Mavericks improve to 2-0 in NBA Cup group play behind a 21-point, 10-rebound, 7-assist night
bullets.note: Dallas is 2-0 in West Group A

bullets.text: Ravens complete a trade for quarterback Jacoby Brissett after their Thursday night loss
bullets.note: Adds a veteran quarterback days before the trade deadline

bullets.text: Ravens not expected to deal RB Derrick Henry before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, sources tell Schefter
bullets.note: Henry is expected to stay in Baltimore through the deadline, per sources

bullets.text: Brandon Aiyuk meets with the 49ers to begin hammering out a path to a split; he says he is healthy and wants reinstatement
bullets.note: A divorce more than two years in the making

bullets.text: Browns will start Shedeur Sanders on Sunday
bullets.note: Reported on NFL Network's The Insiders

bullets.text: 49ers' Nick Bosa and Christian McCaffrey return Sunday; Mike Evans misses a second straight game
bullets.note: San Francisco gets two stars back from calf and hamstring injuries

bullets.text: Seahawks guard Quenton Nelson to have knee surgery but will avoid injured reserve
bullets.note: His timeline is a few weeks, with Seattle's bye in Week 11

bullets.text: Minnesota Wild pick up their 1,000th win in franchise history
bullets.note: Kirill Kaprizov opened the scoring with his league-leading 16th goal

bullets.text: Carlos Alcaraz saves two match points to beat Taylor Fritz 6-7(10), 7-5, 6-3 and reach his first Paris semifinal
bullets.note: He faces Casper Ruud in Saturday's semifinals

bullets.text: Luca Van Assche, 22, beats Rinky Hijikata to become the youngest Frenchman in the Paris semifinals since 2007
bullets.note: His first Masters 1000 semifinal; he faces world No. 4 Ben Shelton next

bullets.text: ATP Finals field set: Zverev, Alcaraz, Shelton, Medvedev, Cobolli, Fils, Tiafoe and Rafael Jodar
bullets.note: Jodar clinched the last spot in a breakthrough first season

recaps.title: Vermont on X
recaps.intro: A soggy, cool weekend is ahead with snow possible on the highest peaks. Burlington's mayoral race got its first major candidate, and a New Hampshire warehouse strike is slowing grocery deliveries in Vermont.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: NWS Burlington: cool, cloudy weekend with rain picking up this afternoon into early Sunday; highs in the 50s
bullets.note: Overnight lows fall into the 40s and 30s

bullets.text: Mountain snow possible this weekend above 2,500 feet, with cold rain showers in the valleys
bullets.note: Snow is expected only at elevations above 2,500 feet

bullets.text: I-89 northbound Exit 9 off-ramp in Middlesex closes Monday, Nov. 9, from 9am to 2:30pm for tree cutting
bullets.note: Plan an alternate route Monday

bullets.text: Some Vermont grocers report delayed deliveries since a New Hampshire warehouse workers strike began Monday
bullets.note: Could mean thinner shelves at some local stores

bullets.text: Burlington City Council President Ben Traverse officially launches his bid for mayor
bullets.note: The Democrat announced Friday after months of speculation

bullets.text: Vermont health insurance open enrollment begins as premiums rise
bullets.note: Enrollment is open now as premiums climb

bullets.text: Vermont advocates celebrate the equal rights amendment victory
bullets.note: Advocates are marking the amendment's win

bullets.text: Seven Days: a required outside audit of Lake Champlain clean water spending, nearing 1 billion dollars, was not done
bullets.note: The cleanup is expected to take 10 more years and another billion dollars
